steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Location factors: proximity to customers/market, transport links, availability of suitable labour, cost of premises, competition, government incentives (grants, enterprise zones).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Business plan: a document setting out the business idea, market research, financial forecasts, marketing strategy. Essential for securing finance from banks or investors. Shows the business has thought through its strategy.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Organic growth: expanding from within - opening new outlets, increasing product range, growing online sales. Slow but controlled, less risky than external growth.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: External growth: mergers (two firms agree to join) and takeovers (one firm buys another). Faster growth but risky: cultural clash, high cost, integration problems. Franchising: rapid expansion with lower capital risk.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain three factors a business should consider when choosing a location for a new factory. | Compare organic growth and external growth as ways for a business to expand. | Explain what is meant by economies of scale and give three examples.

steps.body: Always link location choice to the TYPE of business (retail needs customers; manufacturing needs transport) Distinguish between mergers (agreed) and takeovers (hostile) Explain economies of scale with the 'average cost per unit falls' formula - be precise
